items.title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training

They introduce harness rehearsal—distillation using traces with minimal task content to practice target interfaces—which, when combined with cross-harness task supervision, dramatically improves multi-turn performance. Furthermore, on-policy reinforcement learning is found to be more robust against single-harness performance degradation than distillation.

items.title: Wavefront: Low-Rank Drafting with Parallel Causal Refinement for Speculative Decoding
items.one_liner: Wavefront improves LLM speculative decoding throughput by using low-rank base models with parallel causal refinement correction heads.
items.summary: Wavefront is a novel inference-time method for speculative decoding that addresses token dependence limitations in parallel block drafters by shrinking the base model and strengthening the correction head. By replacing the full lm_head with a learned low-rank base, conditioning the correction head on the entire drafted prefix, and resolving it via parallel Jacobi passes, Wavefront achieves a fixed-budget draft step that is captured as a single CUDA graph in vLLM. items.title: FlashProve-Next: Verifiable Inference for Production LLM APIs
items.one_liner: FlashProve-Next provides verifiable zero-knowledge inference proofs for production LLM APIs without modifying native float serving.
items.summary: FlashProve-Next introduces a verifiable inference system for production LLM APIs that generates zero-knowledge-masked proofs for individual responses without altering native native serving architectures like FlashAttention or bf16/fp8/mxfp4 precision.
